newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Saflife edges up on improved results.
newsitem.headline: Saflife edges up on improved results.

text.p: Shares in South African black empowerment firm Saflife Ltd edged up Monday as the market warmly greeted an improved set of results, dealers said.
"It hasn't set things on fire, but the shares are benefitting from improved figures," one dealer said.
The firm touched a day high of 20.50 rand, before falling back by 0845 GMT to 20.35 rand, up 35 cents. More than 268,000 shares worth 5.47 million rand changed hands.
The group earlier posted earnings per share before exceptionals for the year to March 31 of 98.8 cents, against 72.2 last time.

Saflife, which recently bought South African mining house JCI Ltd, said in a statement with its results that growth potential existed organically and through merger and acquisitions in both the mining and financial service sectors.
The firm said it had paid no dividend so that it could utilise its cash flow income to service its debt.
